clue.text: Form of self-discipline — that's unknown in pirates' home

indicators.note: the unknown is placed inside the form of self-discipline

parts.note: penance is a self-imposed punishment, a form of discipline
Z is a standard algebraic unknown, alongside X and Y

explanation.surface: A monk's austerities seem out of place in a lawless buccaneers' lair.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pirates of Penzance is the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta; Penzance is a town in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera The Pirates of Penzance sets its pirate band in this Cornish town.

clue.text: Play around with quiet Scotsman, losing good husband

parts.note: p is piano, musical notation for quiet

indicators.note: losing means the Scotsman drops these letters

parts.note: a Highlander is a man from the Scottish Highlands
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogies

explanation.surface: A quiet Scot fools around and loses a good husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes GH from HIGHLANDER, leaving HILANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to womanise or have casual affairs is to play around.

clue.text: Oil in container brought up hot? Not quite that

indicators.note: brought up means the container is read upwards, reversed in a down clue

parts.note: a pan is a cooking container
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: Oil heated in a pan, but not quite hot enough.
explanation.walkthrough: PAN read upwards gives NAP; THAT less its last letter gives THA.
explanation.definitionFit: Naphtha is a flammable liquid hydrocarbon distilled from petroleum.

clue.text: Area on floor covering includes black being near to white

indicators.note: includes means the floor covering takes the black letter inside

parts.note: lino is short for linoleum, a floor covering
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils

explanation.surface: A floor covering patterned in black stands near a white one.
explanation.walkthrough: An albino lacks pigment, so is close to white.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or animal lacking pigment has pale skin and hair, close to white.

clue.text: Journalist has line inserted in sloppy miscount

indicators.note: inserted in means the line goes inside the jumbled word
sloppy means the word's letters are carelessly reordered

explanation.surface: A reporter's copy has a line added after a sloppy word count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sloppy' turns MISCOUNT into COUMNIST, and 'inserted in' puts L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A columnist is a writer with a regular newspaper column, so a kind of reporter.

clue.text: Place bringing back Mexican food, cutting the French

indicators.note: the reversed food cuts into the French article, splitting it

parts.note: le is the French masculine for 'the'

indicators.note: bringing back means the food word is read in reverse

parts.note: a taco is a folded Mexican tortilla

explanation.surface: A restaurant sends back Mexican dishes and drops its French menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing back' reverses the food, and 'cutting' splits the French article around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to place something is to find or set its position.

clue.text: Did lash out like a young bloke

indicators.note: out means the letters are sent out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone hit out like a rowdy youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Laddish means behaving boisterously, like a lad or young man.

clue.text: General agreement to deceive public survey reported

parts.note: to con is to deceive

indicators.note: reported means the survey word is heard spoken, so a soundalike spelling is used

parts.note: a census is an official population survey

explanation.surface: A consensus that a public poll is a con.
explanation.walkthrough: CENSUS sounds the same as SENSUS, the end of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad agreement among a whole group of people, a shared opinion.

clue.text: Circus bar where some get high during show

definitions.meaning: a swinging horizontal bar used by acrobats

definitions.text: where some get high during show
definitions.meaning: acrobats swing high above the ring in a circus show

explanation.surface: A circus act where performers get high mid-show.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobats swing from this bar hung from ropes high in the big top.

clue.text: Troublesome child emperor

definitions.meaning: .... is an abbreviation of Imperator, Latin for emperor, seen on Roman coins

explanation.surface: A tantrum-throwing young ruler, like a boy-king.
explanation.definitionFit: A naughty youngster is a little devil, while the Latin title Imperator is abbreviated on coins and inscriptions.

clue.text: Ring girl about party drug

parts.note: to ring is to sound a bell

indicators.note: the girl's name goes about, around, the party

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name
a do is an informal party

explanation.surface: Someone phones a girl about a party where drugs will be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the girl's name around the party word.
explanation.definitionFit: Belladonna, from deadly nightshade, yields atropine, used medicinally as a drug.

clue.text: Self-guiding car not out? I am surprised

parts.note: auto is short for automobile
on a cricket scorecard n.o. stands for not out
'My!' is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A self-driving car that isn't out of the garage provokes surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival but the answer is the noun: 'self-guiding' stands for the state of self-government.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-rule or independence is the state of guiding oneself without outside control.

clue.text: Wild goats mating returned to half of Iberia

indicators.note: half of the word Iberia is its first three letters
returned means the word for mating is read backwards

parts.note: sex, as in mating

explanation.surface: Wild goats come back to Spain and Portugal to breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reads the mating word backwards; 'half of' takes the first three letters of Iberia, which lead the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a mountain goat species with long curved horns found in the Alps and Iberia.

clue.text: Missing what's said when coffee's given out cold

indicators.note: given out means the cold letter is handed out, removed

parts.note: decaf is a coffee without caffeine
C is the standard abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Someone misses the conversation in a café while cold coffee is handed round.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the C (cold) from DECAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot hear misses spoken words, unable to follow speech.

clue.text: Some railways are so enjoyable — no region in particular

definitions.note: adjective: describing railways worked by cable on steep slopes

parts.note: fun means enjoyable

indicators.note: no means the region is removed from the word particular

parts.note: a part is a region or area

explanation.surface: Some railways are fun anywhere, regardless of region.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTICULAR without PART leaves ICULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable-hauled railway climbing a steep slope is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Vineyard business mostly imports large box for bottle

indicators.note: imports means the box is brought inside the shortened business
mostly means the final letter of the business is dropped

parts.note: a winery is a vineyard's wine-making business
a chest is a large box

explanation.surface: A wine-making firm brings in a big crate to hold its bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the business's last letter, leaving WINER, and 'imports' takes the box inside. A Winchester is a large bottle, used in labs for chemicals.
explanation.definitionFit: A Winchester is a large cylindrical container, traditionally holding about half a gallon of liquid or chemical.

clue.text: Oblige those against to be instructed

parts.note: the cons are the arguments against, as in pros and cons
to train is to be taught or instructed, as in train as a nurse

explanation.surface: Opponents are obliged to undergo instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to compel or force someone to act.

clue.text: Passion about English wine which flows from the press?

indicators.note: the passion word goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: rage is violent passion
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Fury at English wine pouring from a wine press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like a wine press; it is the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalistic reporting is the output produced by newspapers.

clue.text: Neither son needs to wave around cheap sparkler

indicators.note: to wave around means the letters of the fodder are flung about into a new order

explanation.surface: Neither son must flash a cheap gem about.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhinestone is an imitation diamond, a glittering paste jewel costing little.

clue.text: What's appropriate in present content of kitchen garden?

indicators.note: the appropriate word goes in the present word

parts.note: here means present
to bag is to appropriate or take

explanation.surface: A question about what goods a kitchen garden contains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like an adjective; it is the verb, to bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbage is grass and green plants, the leafy growth of a vegetable plot.

clue.text: River creatures return about end of August, making fast passage

indicators.note: about means the reversed creatures go round the final letter
return means the creatures' word is read backwards

parts.note: otters live along rivers

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the month

explanation.surface: River animals come back near the end of August.
explanation.walkthrough: OTTERS backwards is SRETTO, with T inside. In music, a stretto is a passage of quicker tempo or overlapping fugue entries.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the term names an accelerated closing section, or overlapping fugal entries.

clue.text: Craft outlet has unit for the old

indicators.note: the unit goes in for, replacing, the old letter

parts.note: a shop is a retail outlet
I is the Roman numeral one, a unit

explanation.surface: A craft shop takes on a unit to replace an old one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like part of 'craft outlet'; it is the definition, a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A seagoing vessel is a craft, as in a small craft afloat.

clue.text: Stop eating regular helpings of big blue fish

indicators.note: eating means the stop word takes the picked letters inside

parts.note: to halt is to stop

indicators.note: regular helpings means every second letter of the two words

explanation.surface: Stop eating regular portions of a big blue fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'big blue' are IBU.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flatfish of northern seas, valued as food.

clue.text: Religious leader followed by the old man of the sea

indicators.note: followed by means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: the Pope leads the Roman Catholic Church
ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: A pontiff followed by an old man of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old man of the sea' looks like a fixed phrase, but 'the old' gives YE. Popeye is the cartoon sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinach-eating cartoon sailor is a seafaring figure.

clue.text: Shopkeeper concerned with dog endlessly returning

indicators.note: returning means the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the dog is dropped

parts.note: a corgi is a small Welsh dog

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper worried that his dog keeps coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves CORG; 'returning' turns the whole string RECORG round.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader who sells food and household goods from a shop.

clue.text: One walking street — bird up for a tumble?

parts.note: the roller is a bird named for its tumbling display flight

explanation.surface: Someone strolling down the road might take a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: Rollers are colourful birds that roll and tumble in courtship flight; tumbler pigeons share the habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taking a leisurely walk is a stroller.

clue.text: With wings wrapping Vermont volume does it

indicators.note: wrapping means the winged word goes around the volume

parts.note: alate means having wings
liter is the American spelling of litre, and Vermont is a US state

explanation.surface: A pun-loving clue that strings W and V sounds together.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue itself repeats W and V sounds, so 'does it' refers to the clue: it does what it says. LITER is the US spelling, signalled by Vermont.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue itself repeats initial sounds, which is what this verb describes.

clue.text: Barman every so often offers cups for women

indicators.note: every so often picks alternate letters of the word, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A barman occasionally hands women cups of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cups' looks like drinking vessels; here they are the cups of underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassiere is the female undergarment with cups for support.

clue.text: Queer fish seen in dam discharge

parts.note: a weir is a low dam across a river
to do a duty is to discharge it

explanation.surface: An odd fish spotted in the water flowing out of a dam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queer fish' here means an eccentric person, not an actual fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an odd or eccentric person is called a queer fish or an oddball.

clue.text: Trouble turning steel nut

indicators.note: turning means the letters are twisted into a new order, as a nut is turned

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to turn a stiff steel nut.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to trouble someone is to disturb or upset them.
